title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Monday, Nov. 9, 2026 · Gambler edition · By Richard J Diskin Jr

paragraphs: Fourteen Week 9 games are final, from Thursday night in Baltimore to Sunday night in Chicago, with a Sunday morning stop in Madrid. The people holding tickets got all of it: a push, a walk-off field goal that settled two numbers at once, a kneel-down that saved an Under, an Under that survived by half a point, a fourth-down stop at the 2 that saved a cover by half a point, and an overtime touchdown that cashed every Over ticket on a game that was 16-16 after regulation.

Graded against the opening lines, the Cover Writer went 5-9 against the spread and 6-8 on the over/under. Graded against the closing lines, the Cover Writer went 5-8-1 against the spread and 9-5 on the over/under.
Bills at Vikings tonight is the last Week 9 game, and it gets graded in Tuesday's edition.

Every side is graded on the team picked and every over/under on the Over or Under called, once against the opening line and once against the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss, and overtime points count. Picks are graded as they stood at kickoff. A few changed in Sunday morning's update before any of those games started, and the ones that mattered are noted where they happened. Each game below opens with both lines and the Cover Writer's card, rides along with the tickets through the plays and flags that swung them, then lists who called it and who missed it.

Opening line: Bears −3.5, over/under 48.5. Closing line: Bears −6.5, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Buccaneers and the Under, projecting Bears 24, Buccaneers 20. Final: Buccaneers 24, Bears 27. The Bears won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

Three handicappers stood with the Cover Writer on the Buccaneers, and everybody with an over/under pick except Follow The Money had the Under. Letdown Watch took the Bears. The game opened Bears −3.5 and closed Bears −6.5, and both numbers came down to the very last snap.

Chicago went up 14-0 in the first quarter on Caleb Williams touchdown throws of 9 yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden III. Then Williams started handing the ball back. An unnecessary roughness flag on Zavion Thomas pushed the Bears from the Tampa Bay 6 back to the 21, and Tykee Smith picked Williams off at the 3. Zyon McCollum intercepted him twice, the second one on a replay reversal of an incompletion. Cam Lewis picked off Baker Mayfield in between, and Chase McLaughlin's 21-yarder on the last play of the half made it Bears 17, Buccaneers 6.

Bucky Irving's 2-yard run at 11:37 of the third got Tampa Bay within 17-13. Alex Anzalone intercepted Williams at 4:38, and on the very next possession Jaylon Johnson picked off Mayfield and went 67 yards the other way. Bears 24, Buccaneers 13. The Buccaneers at the closing +6.5 were 4.5 short, and the Under crowd had 37 points on the board with a quarter to go.

McLaughlin hit from 35 at 11:24 of the fourth. Bears 24, Buccaneers 16, 40 points. At 7:19 the Bears sacked Mayfield back to the Tampa Bay 5 on third-and-8, and a face mask flag on Austin Booker took it off the board. Tampa Bay punted anyway after two more sacks. Then with 3:48 left Burden caught a short pass, Rueben Bain Jr. punched it out, and Ifeatu Melifonwu recovered at the Chicago 21. Irving scored from 6 yards out at 2:51, and Mayfield ran in the two-point try. 24-24. The Buccaneers were covering both numbers, the Under at the closing 47.5 was dead at 48 points, and the Under at the opening 48.5 was alive by half a point.

Then the Bears drove. Colston Loveland caught one for 38 yards to the Tampa Bay 16, Williams knelt twice, and Cairo Santos hit from 38 as time ran out. Bears 27, Buccaneers 24. Chicago played for the field goal instead of the end zone, and that is the only reason the Buccaneers at the opening +3.5 covered by half a point. The same three points put the game at 51 and took the last Under ticket in the building with them.

Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Bears, missed by half a point at the opening Bears −3.5 and missed by 3.5 points at the closing Bears −6.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 48.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 47.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Buccaneers, covered by half a point at the opening Buccaneers +3.5 and covered by 3.5 points at the closing Buccaneers +6.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 48.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 47.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side.

Opening line: 49ers −8.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: 49ers −8.5, over/under 51.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers and the Under, projecting 49ers 31, Raiders 19. Final: Raiders 17, 49ers 38. The 49ers won by 21, and the teams scored 55 points.

The Formula and Letdown Watch had the 49ers with the Cover Writer, Next Man Up took the Raiders, and four of the five had the Under. Follow The Money had the Over. The over/under opened at 46.5 and closed at 51.5, which made the Under a tough ticket at either number and a tougher one at the card's 52.5.

San Francisco led 21-10 at the half. On the Raiders' first play of the third quarter Jaden Dugger intercepted Kirk Cousins and took it 35 yards for a touchdown. 28-10. Brock Bowers caught a 21-yard touchdown at 9:29 to make it 28-17, 45 points. Then Michael Mayer caught a 24-yarder down to the San Francisco 1, Upton Stout knocked it loose, and it went through the end zone for a touchback. Seven points that Under tickets never had to count.

Jordan Watkins caught a 37-yard touchdown from Brock Purdy with 36 seconds left in the third. 35-17, 52 points, and the Under at the closing 51.5 was gone. The card's 52.5 hung on by half a point into the fourth. Mayer caught a 3-yard touchdown at 12:05 that was nullified by his own offensive pass interference flag, and Renardo Green intercepted Cousins in the end zone on the next play. Under backers at 52.5 were thrilled for about seven minutes.

Eddy Pineiro's 35-yarder at 5:21 made it 38-17. Fifty-five points. Malik Mustapha picked off Cousins one more time and Mac Jones knelt it out. The 49ers covered by 12.5 at both numbers, and Follow The Money's Over cashed at both.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Raiders, missed by 12.5 points at the opening Raiders +8.5 and missed by 12.5 points at the closing Raiders +8.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 46.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 51.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the 49ers, covered by 12.5 points at the opening 49ers −8.5 and covered by 12.5 points at the closing 49ers −8.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 46.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 51.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Seahawks −13.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Seahawks −9.5, over/under 39.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Seahawks and the Over, projecting Seahawks 28, Cardinals 18. Final: Cardinals 3, Seahawks 17. The Seahawks won by 14, and the teams scored 20 points.

The Cover Writer went to bed Saturday on the Cardinals +8.5 and woke up Sunday on the Seahawks −8.5, after the morning update flipped the card. The Formula and Letdown Watch had Seattle too, while Next Man Up and Follow The Money stayed with Arizona. Four of the five had the Over. The line opened Seahawks −13.5 and closed −9.5, so the Seattle crowd needed very different things depending on their number.

AJ Barner took a direct snap in from a yard out early in the second quarter. A 29-yard interference flag on Max Melton set up Barner's 7-yard touchdown catch with 15 seconds left in the half, and Jason Myers' 45-yarder at 3:50 of the third made it 17-3. That was the last point of the day. The Over at the closing 39.5 never had a pulse.

The side is where the drama lived. Arizona put together a 14-play, 76-yard drive in the fourth quarter. Josh Jobe intercepted Gardner Minshew II, and Jobe's own interference flag erased it. The Cardinals got to fourth-and-goal at the Seattle 2 at 4:39, and Minshew's throw for Trey McBride fell incomplete. A Cardinals touchdown there makes it 17-10, and every Seattle ticket at −13.5, −9.5 or −8.5 loses. Instead Seattle knelt it out.

Seattle by 14. The Seahawks at the opening −13.5 covered by half a point, thanks to a fourth-down stop at the 2. The Cover Writer's flip from Arizona to Seattle cashed, and the Under that only Follow The Money had cashed by 19.5 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Cardinals, missed by half a point at the opening Cardinals +13.5 and missed by 4.5 points at the closing Cardinals +9.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over, fell short by 25.5 points at the opening 45.5 and fell short by 19.5 points at the closing 39.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Seahawks, covered by half a point at the opening Seahawks −13.5 and covered by 4.5 points at the closing Seahawks −9.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 25.5 points at the opening 45.5 and stayed under by 19.5 points at the closing 39.5.
No pick: In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Patriots −1.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Patriots −3, over/under 45. The Cover Writer's card had the Patriots and the Under, projecting Patriots 24, Packers 20. Final: Packers 45, Patriots 27. The Packers won by 18, and the teams scored 72 points.

This one is going on the Cover Writer's blooper reel. The card had the Packers +3.5 right up until Sunday morning's update flipped it to the Patriots −3.5. The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money were on New England too. Next Man Up kept the Packers. Everybody with an over/under pick had the Under.

On New England's second snap Xavier McKinney intercepted Drake Maye, and Jordan Love scrambled 13 yards for a touchdown two plays later. Love hit Matthew Golden from 5 yards out, and it was 14-0 before eight minutes were gone. McKinney picked Maye off again in the second quarter, and the Packers led 24-14 at the half. Thirty-eight points at halftime, and the Under at 45 had a very long third quarter coming.

Love hit Savion Williams for a 10-yard touchdown at 10:51 to make it 45 points, and Trey Smack's 51-yarder at 5:13 pushed it past every number on the board. Then Love threw 39 yards to Christian Watson and ran in the two-point try himself. Packers 42, Patriots 14. The Under was finished before the fourth quarter started, and so were the Patriots tickets.
Packers 45, Patriots 27. New England at −3 lost by 21. The Packers at +3.5, the side the Cover Writer gave up a few hours before kickoff, covered by 21.5. Next Man Up gets this one all to itself.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Patriots, missed by 19.5 points at the opening Patriots −1.5 and missed by 21 points at the closing Patriots −3; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Under, went over by 25.5 points at the opening 46.5 and went over by 27 points at the closing 45.
Called it at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Packers, covered by 19.5 points at the opening Packers +1.5 and covered by 21 points at the closing Packers +3.
No pick: In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Chargers −2.5, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Texans −5.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chargers and the Over, projecting Texans 22, Chargers 19. Final: Texans 44, Chargers 22. The Texans won by 22, and the teams scored 66 points.

The Cover Writer and all four handicappers with a side took the Chargers, and the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch had the Over. In The Trenches had the Under. The side went from Chargers −2.5 at the open to Texans −5.5 at the close, so the market had stopped believing long before kickoff.

C.J. Stroud threw touchdowns of 17 yards to Xavier Hutchinson, 63 to Tank Dell and 12 to Kayshon Boutte in the first half, and Houston led 24-9. Nico Collins caught a 13-yarder in the third. When Stroud found Boutte again for 63 yards early in the fourth quarter it was 38-9, 47 points, and the Over had cashed at both numbers with almost a full quarter to spare.
Texans 44, Chargers 22. Houston by 22, the Chargers missed by 16.5 at the close, and 66 points went over the closing 40.5 by 25.5. In The Trenches had a long afternoon.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Chargers, missed by 24.5 points at the opening Chargers −2.5 and missed by 16.5 points at the closing Chargers +5.5; In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 22.5 points at the opening 43.5 and went over by 25.5 points at the closing 40.5.
Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over, went over by 22.5 points at the opening 43.5 and went over by 25.5 points at the closing 40.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Chiefs −9.5, over/under 41.5. Closing line: Chiefs −9, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Jets and the Under, projecting Chiefs 25, Jets 18. Final: Jets 12, Chiefs 35. The Chiefs won by 23, and the teams scored 47 points.

The Formula and Next Man Up joined the Cover Writer on the Jets plus the points, Letdown Watch took the Chiefs, and four of the five pickers had the Under. Follow The Money had the Over. The over/under opened at 41.5 and closed at 47.5, a 6-point climb, and the Under at the closing number hung by a thread all afternoon.

Jason Sanders kicked the Jets to four first-half field goals, from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards, and Kenneth Walker III caught two touchdown passes from Patrick Mahomes. Then the half ended in a kicking clinic of the wrong kind. Sanders missed a 53-yarder wide left with 37 seconds left. Harrison Butker's 56-yarder hit the right upright, an offside flag on Malik McClain gave him another shot, and he missed that one from 51. Chiefs 14, Jets 12 at halftime.

Travis Kelce scored on fourth-and-goal from the 1 at 10:20 of the third, and Walker ran one in from 2 yards with 11 seconds left in the quarter. 28-12, 40 points. Emmett Johnson's 6-yard run at 3:35 of the fourth made it 35-12, 47 points, half a point under the closing 47.5.

From there every Under ticket needed nobody to score for three and a half minutes. The Jets went for it on fourth-and-9 at the Kansas City 37 and Geno Smith threw incomplete. The Chiefs ran Jaydn Ott three times and Justin Fields knelt at the New York 44. Under 47.5 cashed by half a point. The Jets at +9 lost by 14.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Jets, missed by 13.5 points at the opening Jets +9.5 and missed by 14 points at the closing Jets +9.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 5.5 points at the opening 41.5 and stayed under by half a point at the closing 47.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 5.5 points at the opening 41.5 and fell short by half a point at the closing 47.5.
Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Chiefs, covered by 13.5 points at the opening Chiefs −9.5 and covered by 14 points at the closing Chiefs −9.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Cowboys −1.5, over/under 52.5. Closing line: Cowboys −4, over/under 51.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Colts and the Under, projecting Colts 27, Cowboys 24. Final: Cowboys 27, Colts 23. The Cowboys won by 4, and the teams scored 50 points.

Every handicapper with a side was on the Colts, and the over/under split three for the Under to two for the Over. The side opened Cowboys −1.5 and closed Cowboys −4, which turned the last two minutes into three different results for three different tickets.

Dallas led 17-7 at the half and should have been up more in the third. CeeDee Lamb's 11-yard touchdown catch at 3:04 was reversed by replay, and the Cowboys settled for Brandon Aubrey's 28-yarder. That reversal took four points off the board, and Under tickets will want to send the replay booth a thank-you note.

Then the fourth quarter turned into a kicking contest. Spencer Shrader tied it 20-20 with a 59-yarder at 5:56. Aubrey missed from 50 wide left at 3:34. Shrader hit from 50 at 1:37, and the Colts led 23-20. Every Colts ticket on the board was cashing.

It lasted less than half a minute. Dak Prescott hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards to the Indianapolis 19, an illegal use of hands flag and an interference flag on Kapena Gushiken moved the ball to the 1, and Javonte Williams scored at 1:08. Cowboys 27, Colts 23. Caleb Downs intercepted Daniel Jones to end it. Dallas by 4: the Colts at the opening +1.5 lost by 2.5, the Colts at the closing +4 pushed, and the card's +5.5 cashed. Fifty points stayed under at both numbers.
Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 2.5 points at the opening 52.5 and fell short by 1.5 points at the closing 51.5.

Missed at the opening number, pushed at the closing: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Colts, missed by 2.5 points at the opening Colts +1.5 and pushed at the closing Colts +4.
Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Under, stayed under by 2.5 points at the opening 52.5 and stayed under by 1.5 points at the closing 51.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Saints −3.5, over/under 41.5. Closing line: Saints −4.5, over/under 43.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Browns and the Over, projecting Saints 22, Browns 21. Final: Browns 22, Saints 23 in overtime. The Saints won by 1, and the teams scored 45 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch had the Browns and the Over. Next Man Up started the week there too, then flipped to the Saints and the Under in Sunday morning's update. Hold that thought.

This was 6-6 going into the fourth quarter, and Over tickets at 43.5 were reading the obituaries. Charlie Smyth's 48-yarder at 5:38 put the Saints up 9-6. On the very next snap Shedeur Sanders hit KC Concepcion for 64 yards and a touchdown, 13-9 Browns. Audric Estime's 2-yard run with 58 seconds left made it 16-13 Saints, and Andre Szmyt answered with a 51-yarder at 0:08. Regulation ended 16-16, 32 points, and the Over at the closing 43.5 needed 12 more in overtime.

It got 13. Tyler Shough hit Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown, Saints 23-16. Sanders came right back and found Harold Fannin Jr. for 39 yards and a touchdown with a minute left, and the Browns went for two and the win. The try to Denzel Boston fell incomplete. Saints 23, Browns 22.

So the Saints won and the Browns covered every number on the board, and the overtime touchdowns cashed the Over at the opening 41.5 and the closing 43.5. Next Man Up's original card, the Browns and the Over, cashed both pieces. The one it switched to lost both.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Saints, missed by 2.5 points at the opening Saints −3.5 and missed by 3.5 points at the closing Saints −4.5; Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Under, went over by 3.5 points at the opening 41.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 43.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Browns, covered by 2.5 points at the opening Browns +3.5 and covered by 3.5 points at the closing Browns +4.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over, went over by 3.5 points at the opening 41.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 43.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Broncos −3, over/under 42.5. Closing line: Broncos −3, over/under 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers and the Over, projecting Broncos 24, Panthers 22. Final: Broncos 26, Panthers 21. The Broncos won by 5, and the teams scored 47 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up had the Panthers plus the points. Letdown Watch took the Broncos. Every handicapper with an over/under pick, Follow The Money included, had the Over. The line sat at Broncos −3 from open to close.

Carolina led 14-13 into the fourth. Jonah Coleman's 9-yard run at 10:17 put Denver ahead 19-14, and the two-point try failed. Bo Nix hit Pat Bryant for a 26-yard touchdown at 5:41. Broncos 26, Panthers 14, 40 points. Panthers +3 needed more than a touchdown, and the Over at the closing 44.5 needed one.

Bryce Young went for it on fourth-and-18 from the Denver 34 and hit John Metchie III for 25 yards, and a roughing the passer flag on Zach Allen moved it to the 4. Young found Tetairoa McMillan for the touchdown at 3:05. 26-21, 47 points. That cashed the Over at both numbers, for everybody.

The Panthers got the ball back down 5 with a chance to win it. Nik Bonitto strip-sacked Young at 1:24 and recovered it himself, and the replay held up. Broncos by 5. The Panthers at +3 missed by 2 at both numbers, and Letdown Watch took the side by itself.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Panthers, missed by 2 points at the opening Panthers +3 and missed by 2 points at the closing Panthers +3.

Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Broncos, covered by 2 points at the opening Broncos −3 and covered by 2 points at the closing Broncos −3; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 4.5 points at the opening 42.5 and went over by 2.5 points at the closing 44.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Rams −5.5, over/under 50.5. Closing line: Rams −4.5, over/under 48. The Cover Writer's card had the Rams and the Under, projecting Rams 26, Commanders 21. Final: Rams 20, Commanders 13. The Rams won by 7, and the teams scored 33 points.
The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches had the Rams. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money had Washington. Next Man Up had the only Over. The Rams opened −5.5 and closed −4.5.
It was 13-13 after three quarters, and Puka Nacua's 7-yard touchdown at 12:51 of the fourth made it 20-13. Rams −4.5 needed that to hold, and Washington backers needed one touchdown.

Washington got the ball back in the final minute and moved it. On the final snap Jayden Daniels hit Chig Okonkwo for 20 yards to the Rams 11, Jaylen McCollough knocked it loose, Rachaad White scooped it up and lost it again, and Byron Young fell on it. Rams 20, Commanders 13. A Washington touchdown on that play beats the Rams −4.5 and −5.5. The Rams covered by 1.5 at the open and 2.5 at the close, and 33 points sailed under both numbers.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Commanders, missed by 1.5 points at the opening Commanders +5.5 and missed by 2.5 points at the closing Commanders +4.5; Next Man Up on the Over, fell short by 17.5 points at the opening 50.5 and fell short by 15 points at the closing 48.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on the Rams, covered by 1.5 points at the opening Rams −5.5 and covered by 2.5 points at the closing Rams −4.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 17.5 points at the opening 50.5 and stayed under by 15 points at the closing 48.
No pick: Follow The Money on the over/under.

Opening line: Lions −6.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Lions −6.5, over/under 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins and the Under, projecting Lions 27, Dolphins 22. Final: Lions 19, Dolphins 9. The Lions won by 10, and the teams scored 28 points.
The Cover Writer and three handicappers had the Dolphins plus the points and the Under. The line was Lions −6.5 at the open and at the close.

Miami nearly had a 72-yard fumble return for a touchdown by Jordyn Brooks in the first quarter, and replay took it away. Zane Gonzalez's 38-yarder hit the right upright with 3 seconds left in the half. Jahmyr Gibbs went 8 yards for a touchdown on fourth-and-1 late in the third, and Detroit led 16-6.

The Dolphins had first-and-goal at the Detroit 7 early in the fourth. Alim McNeill sacked Malik Willis for 9 yards and Derrick Moore sacked him for 3 more, and Gonzalez kicked a 34-yarder. 16-9. A touchdown there makes it 16-13, with the Dolphins covering. Instead the Dolphins at +6.5 were missing by half a point, and then Jake Bates hit from 43 at 4:28 to make it 19-9. The Dolphins missed by 3.5. The Under cashed by a mile, 28 points against 50.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Dolphins, missed by 3.5 points at the opening Dolphins +6.5 and missed by 3.5 points at the closing Dolphins +6.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, stayed under by 19.5 points at the opening 47.5 and stayed under by 22.5 points at the closing 50.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Eagles −5.5, over/under 44.5. Closing line: Giants −3, over/under 37.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Eagles and the Over, projecting Giants 22, Eagles 21. Final: Giants 19, Eagles 11. The Giants won by 8, and the teams scored 30 points.

The Cover Writer and four handicappers had the Eagles plus the points and the Over. Follow The Money skipped the side and took the Under. This game opened Eagles −5.5 and closed Giants −3, and the over/under dropped 7 points to 37.5.

Dominic Zvada kicked four field goals for the Giants, including a 49-yarder at 4:24 of the fourth that made it 19-8. Jake Elliott hit from 45 at 1:56 to make it 19-11, and Malik Nabers fell on the onside kick.

The Eagles still got one more shot from their own 5 with 1:32 left. Joe Milton got them only as far as their own 44, and on the last play of the game Darius Alexander sacked him. Giants 19, Eagles 11. The Eagles at +3 needed a touchdown, and the Over at 37.5 needed a touchdown plus the two-point try. Follow The Money's Under cashed by 7.5 at the close and 14.5 at the open.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Eagles, missed by 13.5 points at the opening Eagles −5.5 and missed by 5 points at the closing Eagles +3; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 14.5 points at the opening 44.5 and fell short by 7.5 points at the closing 37.5.
Called it at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 14.5 points at the opening 44.5 and stayed under by 7.5 points at the closing 37.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side.

Opening line: Bengals −4.5, over/under 49.5. Closing line: Bengals −3.5, over/under 52.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Falcons and the Under, projecting Bengals 25, Falcons 23. Final: Bengals 34, Falcons 17. The Bengals won by 17, and the teams scored 51 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up went with the Falcons, Letdown Watch took the Bengals, and all four had the Under. The over/under opened at 49.5 and closed at 52.5, so the same Under ticket could be a winner or a loser depending on when it was bought.

Ja'Marr Chase took one 47 yards to the end zone, Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns, and Evan McPherson hit a 57-yarder with 24 seconds left in the half. Bengals 24, Falcons 10 at the break, 34 points. Higgins's second touchdown, at 2:05 of the third, made it 31-17 and put 48 points on the board.

That is where the Under sweat started. Atlanta had third-and-2 at the Cincinnati 10, a holding flag on Kyle Pitts Sr. backed the Falcons up to the 20, and Nick Folk missed the 38-yarder wide left at 11:31 of the fourth. McPherson's 43-yarder at 4:36 made it 34-17, 51 points, and that killed the Under at the opening 49.5. Barrett Carter then intercepted Michael Penix Jr., and the Bengals drove to first-and-goal at the Atlanta 8 in the final minutes.

One more Bengals touchdown there makes it 58 points and sinks the Under at the closing 52.5 too. Joe Burrow took a knee at 0:39. Under tickets at 52.5 survived by 1.5 because Cincinnati decided it had enough, and because Folk's kick went left.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Falcons, missed by 12.5 points at the opening Falcons +4.5 and missed by 13.5 points at the closing Falcons +3.5.
Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 1.5 points at the opening 49.5 and stayed under by 1.5 points at the closing 52.5.
Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Bengals, covered by 12.5 points at the opening Bengals −4.5 and covered by 13.5 points at the closing Bengals −3.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Ravens −4.5, over/under 49.5. Closing line: Jaguars −9.5, over/under 40. The Cover Writer's card had the Ravens and the Over, projecting Jaguars 25, Ravens 20. Final: Jaguars 33, Ravens 10. The Jaguars won by 23, and the teams scored 43 points.
The Cover Writer and three handicappers had the Ravens plus the points and the Over. This line went from Ravens −4.5 at the open to Jaguars −9.5 at the close, and the over/under fell from 49.5 to 40.

Trevor Lawrence hit Parker Washington for a 50-yard touchdown before the half, Montaric Brown and Jourdan Lewis each picked off Joe Fagnano, and Cam Little kicked field goals from 36, 45, 47 and 33. Chris Rodriguez Jr. took a direct snap in from 2 yards at 7:26 of the fourth. Jaguars 33, Ravens 3, and 36 points on the board. The Ravens tickets were long gone, and the Over at the closing 40 needed a touchdown.

Eleven seconds later it got one. Justice Hill ran 65 yards for a Baltimore touchdown on the first snap after the kickoff. Jaguars 33, Ravens 10, 43 points. That run cashed the Over at the closing 40 by 3 and the card's 39.5 by 3.5. It did nothing for anybody at the opening 49.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Ravens, missed by 27.5 points at the opening Ravens −4.5 and missed by 13.5 points at the closing Ravens +9.5.
Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over, fell short by 6.5 points at the opening 49.5 and went over by 3 points at the closing 40.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer missed 17 times and hit 11 times at the opening lines, and missed 13 times and hit 14 times at the closing lines, with one push and Monday night still to come.

The Cover Writer is 5-9 against the spread at the open and 5-8-1 at the close, and 6-8 on the over/under at the open and 9-5 at the close. The Sunday morning update giveth and taketh away. Flipping off the Cardinals and onto the Seahawks cashed. Flipping off the Packers +3.5 and onto the Patriots −3.5 turned into a 45-27 Green Bay win, which is the kind of thing that gets brought up at every meeting from now until Christmas. Tonight the card has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under 45.5.

The Formula is 5-9 against the spread at the open and 5-8-1 at the close, and 6-8 on the over/under at the open and 9-5 at the close. The Formula and the Cover Writer went pick for pick on all 14 games, so they own every win and every loss together, including the Patriots. Tonight they finally split up: The Formula has the Bills −3.5 and the Over, projecting Bills 27, Vikings 19, so one of them is going to be insufferable on Tuesday.

Next Man Up is 2-12 against the spread at the open and 2-11-1 at the close, and 3-11 on the over/under at the open and 6-8 at the close. It was a rough week, and the Saints game is the one to frame. Next Man Up had the Browns and the Over, switched to the Saints and the Under on Sunday morning, and watched the Browns cover and the game go over in overtime. The Packers +3.5 call is the bright spot, and nobody else in the room had it at kickoff. Tonight Next Man Up has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under.

Letdown Watch is 6-8 against the spread at the open and 6-7-1 at the close, and 6-8 on the over/under at the open and 9-5 at the close. Letdown Watch took the Bears on Sunday night and got the Bears, just not by 7. Over the last two weeks Letdown Watch is 16-12 against the spread at the open, the best mark in the room on the side, and it would like that mentioned before anybody brings up the over/under. Tonight it has the Vikings +3.5 and the Over.

Follow The Money is 0-3 against the spread at both numbers, and 6-2 on the over/under at the open and 5-3 at the close. Follow The Money made three side picks, Washington, New England and Arizona, and all three lost. The over/under is a different story, and the Giants-Eagles Under cashed by 14.5 at the open. Follow The Money sits out tonight, which means it gets to spend Monday night telling everybody what the market was saying.

In The Trenches is 2-3 against the spread at the open and 2-2-1 at the close, and 1-4 on the over/under at both numbers. In The Trenches pulled out of eight games in Sunday morning's update, and two of the cards it walked away from, the Browns with the Over and the Packers with the Over, would have cashed both pieces. The Buccaneers +6.5 and the Rams were the wins that stayed on the card. Tonight it has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under.

The card has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under 45.5, projecting Bills 24, Vikings 21. The Formula has the Bills −3.5 and the Over, projecting Bills 27, Vikings 19. Next Man Up has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under, projecting Bills 23, Vikings 22. Letdown Watch has the Vikings +3.5 and the Over, projecting Vikings 25, Bills 24. In The Trenches has the Vikings +3.5 and the Under, projecting Bills 22, Vikings 20. Follow The Money has no pick.

Four of the five pickers on the side have the Vikings, and the over/under splits three for the Under to two for the Over. Buffalo by exactly 3 is the finish to watch: a push for anybody holding Vikings +3 and a win at +3.5. And with the over/under down 5 points since the open, the Over crowd is already working uphill.

ESPN lists Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray out with a hamstring injury, along with wide receiver Jauan Jennings and running back Demond Claiborne. The card went up on Nov. 4, when Murray was listed as the expected starter. Buffalo has wide receivers Tyrell Shavers and Joshua Palmer out, and tackles Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson questionable. Josh Allen has thrown for 1,793 yards and 11 touchdowns, James Cook III has 707 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns, and Greg Rousseau has 7 sacks.
